A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the self-report Charlson comorbidity index (SR-CCI), but not medical record-based CCl (MR-CCI), was associated with lower health-related quality of Life (HRQoI).
the SR-CCI was moderately associated with the MR-CCIs, and that the SR-CCIs, but not the MR-CCls, were independently associated with poorer HRQoL in Asian patients with RA.
the SR-CCI demonstrated good concordance with a MR-CCI, but only the former instrument was associated with lower HRQL scores.
The main takeaway from our work is that
self-report is a valid and reliable tool for assessing comorbidities in patients with rheumatic disease.
the Charlson Comorbidities Index derived from self-reported information may be a useful tool in clinical settings and research studies involving Asian patients with rheumatology diseases.
there is a need to improve methods of assessing comorbidities in rheumatology patients.
